**8** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/activity-read-visibility.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-log-read-visibility.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/credential-use-audit.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/activity-read-visibility.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-log-read-visibility.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/credential-use-audit.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bfbcd81fbaa2f7b4d6c65e896d98b80cbd891133` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `88d275ae100f468498421a5c11adde6a6e53bd74` — the merge of head `e44d3ca315a96ebc9b1a85a6924930d19b69e82e` into base `bfbcd81fbaa2f7b4d6c65e896d98b80cbd891133`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 88d275ae100f468498421a5c11adde6a6e53bd74 && git checkout 88d275ae100f468498421a5c11adde6a6e53bd74
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bfbcd81fbaa2f7b4d6c65e896d98b80cbd891133 e44d3ca315a96ebc9b1a85a6924930d19b69e82e && git checkout -B drift-repro bfbcd81fbaa2f7b4d6c65e896d98b80cbd891133 && git merge --no-ff e44d3ca315a96ebc9b1a85a6924930d19b69e82e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bfbcd81fbaa2f7b4d6c65e896d98b80cbd891133
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c3027654d4ae85ce1834e5e677235f1d3044fc4b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/parent-record-read-gate.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/comment-access-hooks.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/activity-read-visibility.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-log-read-visibility.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/credential-use-audit.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/activity-read-visibility.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-log-read-visibility.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/comment-read-visibility.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/comment-thread-leaf.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/parent-record-read-admission.integration.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/activity-parent-read-gate.dogfood.test.ts + packages/spec/src/data/api-derivation.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/activity-field-redaction.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts, packages/spec/src/security/capabilities.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-oauth-consent.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-session.object.ts, .changeset/activity-parent-read-matches-data-door.md

Inputs read: the PR body, its 12-file list, all four comments (docs-drift 6823443797, claim 6837421689, os-dev report 6838774373, review claim 6838857481), the net diff from merge-base `d094752f6a` to the head, and the check-runs on the head. Nothing was built, run or re-run. Surfaces other than the three gates the ruling names were not judged.

### ① Derived judgments

Rule under review: a row about a record is served only when the reader can open that record through the data door.

- Accept-set, activity stream: narrowed for every non-system reader to rows whose parent object the data door serves `get` for. RIGHT. The predicate is the spec's one exposure decision (`canServeApiOperation` in `packages/spec/src/data/api-derivation.ts`), the same decision the data door's enforcement reads through `apiExposureDenialReason` in `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`; it takes no caller, so the answer is the same for every reader.
- Accept-set, compliance ledger: narrowed the same way for every reader the gate narrows; a holder of the ledger's audit capability is decided before the gate and keeps every row. RIGHT, and it agrees with the published description of that capability in `packages/spec/src/security/capabilities.ts` ("records the holder cannot open"), which needs no change.
- Accept-set, ledger rows about no record (the gate's outside class): unchanged. RIGHT: the rule speaks of rows about a record, and that class carries no record id.
- Accept-set, comments: narrowed on stamped rows (the shared enumeration) and on unstamped rows (the thread probe). RIGHT. Reactions follow, since their gate reads comments as the caller.
- Accept-set, list-only parents: an object that grants `list` and not `get` is treated as not served. RIGHT against the rule as ruled (the reader must be able to OPEN the record), and it is declared in the changeset.
- Accept-set, no registry view: the whole-read probe and the thread probe keep no row. RIGHT (fail closed), and reported once per engine and seam.
- Accept-set, system reads, internal reads, `canReadObject`, the engine's leaf: unchanged. RIGHT: the predicate is applied only in the gate's enumeration and its two probes.
- Public surface: none added or removed. The two new functions are exported from the module only, not from the package entry; no schema key, no error code, no route, no capability description moves.
- Gate verdicts: every check-run on the head is success or an expected skip (Test Core 8 of 8, the four Type Check runs, the Lint family, Dogfood Regression Gate, Live E2E UI, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness).

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-audit: patch` with a BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on both the PR body and the changeset, plus one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required`, no migration prescription). CORRECT under AGENTS.md, after-task step 3: nothing an author can write changes, so the kind is `none` and the level is `patch`; a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` and keeps its banner and its ADR-0087 disposition. Only `plugin-audit` publishes a change; the dogfood package change is a test. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- PR author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.
- os-dev report 6838774373: `open_questions` is empty, `security_findings` is none, `out_of_scope_findings` is empty. Nothing to answer or escalate.
- Hand-over flag (claim 6837421689): the items the previous holder left unmeasured were re-measured in report 6838774373 on the merge of this head with `main`; the head itself did not move. Answered.
- Docs-drift comment 6823443797: three changed files yielded no anchor. Their changes on this head are header comments only (`activity-read-visibility.ts`, `audit-log-read-visibility.ts`, `credential-use-audit.ts`). Answered; see nit 2 for the one page that restates the ledger rule.
- `Skills-docs: none`: holds; no published skill names these gates.
- The PR is a draft; that is a landing state, not a review flag.

### ④ Design judgment

Against the ruling of record (the activity stream, the audit log and comments are all judged by the data door):

- `parent-record-read-gate.ts`. Holds. The door decision sits in `enumerateParentObjects`, which is the single source of both the leaves and the restricted probe's parents (`planParentReads` builds both from it), so the comment "a restricted probe's parents are enumerated, so the data door serves each" is true of the code. The whole-read probe takes its allow-set from the registry's door-served objects and from nothing when no registry view exists. A read whose own `where` names only a parent the door does not serve gets no branch, hence the deny-all sentinel or the outside class alone. The gate's exemption is still decided first. Tried to break: a named parent re-admitted past the door (no: `namedParents` only lifts the audit-writer exclusion, the door check still runs on it); a probe parent that skipped the enumeration (none); divergence between the registry's `enable` and the door's (the registry's rewrite in `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` strips write verbs only, so `get` is judged alike); a non-machine object name (dropped before the check on every path). The module header's new section agrees with the code sentence by sentence.
- `comment-access-hooks.ts`. Holds. Stamped rows go through the shared gate; the unstamped-thread probe now drops a thread whose object is not door-served before any caller-scoped read, on both the unstamped-only and the undeclared-pair path. The engine parameter type is widened to the registry-bearing engine type and both call sites already pass it.
- `activity-read-visibility.ts`, `audit-log-read-visibility.ts`, `credential-use-audit.ts`. Header comments only; each sentence matches the code. The consent object named in the credential-use header does refuse every operation in its declaration; the session object named as a ledger parent grants `get`, so sign-in rows keep their existing rule.
- `activity-field-redaction.ts` (unchanged, cited by the PR body). The claim holds: it reads the same enumeration, so it writes no branch for an excluded parent.
- Tests. The integration describe runs a real engine and driver, opens with a non-vacuity control, covers leaf and probe paths for all three gates by list, count, aggregate and findOne, and carries controls for a served parent, a parent with no `enable` block and a capability holder. The unit files pin the leaf path, the whole-read probe, the list-only case and the once-only warning. The dogfood case asserts the parent's own door answer beside the row's, for a member and an administrator. They test the rule, not the implementation's shape.

Findings:

1. nit — the changeset says rows about every other object are served exactly as before; on an engine with no registry view the probes now serve none (fail closed). The PR body says so, the changeset does not. Prose face; fix there or leave.
2. nit — `content/docs/permissions/record-view-auditing.mdx` restates the ledger read rule as "the caller can read the record it names". It stays true as a necessary condition, but does not say that the record must be one the data door opens. Follow-up card, not this head.
3. nit — the door-served set is rebuilt from the whole registry on each probed read, and twice on a comment read. Cost only, no effect on the answer. Accepted deviation; a fix would move the head.

No must-fix, no should-fix.
